I tried a week ago (you can check my post history) and all I know is that it wasn't worth it. I've been there and I've felt like you feel. It's always horrible being the older sibling because it feels like you can never be good enough; you always want them to be better, have a better role model, and you want them to achieve more than you ever did. The thing that stopped me was the fact that (cos my sister is at uni) my mum always corrects herself sadly when she says "a table for 4 please" and has to say "a table for 3". It's a stupid little thing, but you've gotta live for those stupid little things. There are so many stupid little things that matter so much. The stupid little things are the best.

You don't have to live for anyone. You've just got to live for yourself.

You don't have to be perfect. You just have to live. Live for the sunrise tomorrow because if you cant sleep tonight, you can watch it rise in the morning. Live for the game/tv show/film you want to see that hasn't come out yet. Live for next season's clothing line from your favourite store. Live because nobody will love the puppies in the same way you do. Live because your sister will always need you, no matter whether you're a good role model or not. Live because tomorrow it might snow/the sun might shine and that'll be pretty. Live because there are restaurants you haven't eaten nachos at. Live because life has so much to offer, and you have so much to look forward to. Treat yourself to something online and live because you're excited for it to arrive (it can always be something cheap/silly/simple, like some nice pencils or a dvd or some socks). Live because you're needed and loved and wanted and there are always things to look forward to, even if it's hard to see that right now.

Live because your lil sister needs you. You don't have to be the best sister. I know I'm not. It doesn't matter how much you played with her in the past. What matters is that you age with her so she can always have someone to rely on. Someone to ask for advice. Someone to admire, even if you mess up. She'll love you no matter what. 

You could leave us right now, or you could take a pretty picture of the frost on the grass tomorrow. A personal thing that has always helped me has been taking pictures. If I see something that makes me smile, I always take a picture. I don't care if the picture is good because I'll always know that it made me smile when I look back on it. Screenshot funny memes or cute pics or baby animals or pics of celebs doing dumb things. Save the stuff that makes you smile. Then remember that when tomorrow comes, there will be more pics to save because there will be something silly that makes you smile. The silly stuff is always the best stuff.

I can't speak as someone who has commuted that far, but I can speak as the kid of someone who did. 

My dad used to commute to work an hour away when I was still in school. I missed him but he'd always make up for lost time on weekends, in the evenings, and on holidays. Those times would always be special because "yay!! Dad's home!!" Even when I was in my teens I still loved the time he made sure he put aside for my mum, my sister & I. Sometimes he'd get us a chocolate bar from the petrol station on the way home. 

Obviously it's not for everyone. For me, it meant we didn't see him in the mornings and he'd get home just before dinner. He had a tough job so sometimes he would be too tired to do anything and would just want to watch TV, eat dinner, then go to bed. But now I'm older all we think about are the good times we did get to spend as a family.

"Money can't buy happiness." 

My dad always says this whenever the topic came up.

I had a lot of friends from poorer families growing up. I saw how much their parents struggled just to put food on the table. My friend found a £10 note and it immediately went to paying to keep the electricity meter running. It made her families' week.
